execution_overview.overall_summary: Executed Python translations for Task1 and Task2 inside Docker. Task1 regression without intercept shows wage gain decreasing with more schooling (vNS > vSHS > vHSD > vSC), supporting the claim. Task2 joint F-test for vSHS=vHSD=vSC=0 failed to reject (F≈0.403, p≈0.751), suggesting inconclusive evidence despite point estimates aligning with the claim.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Followed the planned path with country FEs and schooling dummies; only metadata repair and Python translation were performed.

test_statistics.other: Coefficients (no intercept): vNS=39229 (p=0.00061), vSHS=31905 (p=0.00917), vHSD=24465 (p=0.0514), vSC=19528 (p=0.292). Country FE included; MEX negative and significant.

result_raw.result_text: Estimated wage gain is largest for no-schooling and decreases with higher schooling categories; vNS and vSHS are significant and larger than vHSD and vSC.

conclusion.conclusion_text: Results support the focal claim: wage gains at migration decrease as schooling increases.

result_raw.result_text: Joint F-test for vSHS=vHSD=vSC=0 is not significant (p≈0.751). Point estimates are directionally consistent with larger gains for less schooling, but not statistically significant.

conclusion.conclusion_text: The joint test fails to reject that differences by schooling (excluding no school) are zero; evidence regarding the focal claim is inconclusive in this specification.
